sections.html:
One house can produce two separate bills. Johnson City's Finance Department mails the city bill and collects that payment, while the Washington County Trustee handles the county tax on the same parcel. The city's property tax page names the Municipal and Safety Building at 601 E. Main St. as the walk-in counter, open weekdays eight to five. Mailed checks belong at Box 2227, Johnson City, TN 37605, and the tax office at 423-434-6299 answers questions about late balances.

For the county bill, the Assessor of Property (423-753-1671) answers appraisal and mailing address questions. The Trustee (423-753-1602) collects and nothing more; appraisals and rates are not its job.

Most of the city lies in Washington County, though small parts reach into Carter and Sullivan counties. Houses in those parts deal with that other county's assessor and trustee, so check the county shown on your parcel record before you pick up the phone.

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
The 2026 city bill must be paid by February 28, 2027, and a postmark dated that day still counts. Penalty and interest start March 1, 2027. County timing is close: the Trustee mails notices in October, accepts payment until the end of February, then adds 1.5% interest to what is left on March 1.

In Tennessee the duty to pay does not depend on getting a notice. Homeowners whose lender pays from escrow receive no bill and should ask the servicer for proof of payment. Anyone still waiting on a county notice by mid November should call the Trustee.

Ways to pay the city portion:

  • In person at 601 E. Main St. during weekday hours
  • By mail to the P.O. Box above
  • Online through the Finance Department's payment system, which adds a 2.75% processing fee per transaction

Once an account is delinquent, the online system will not take it, and the same goes for taxes already filed in Chancery Court. Dial 423-434-6299 for an exact payoff before you send anything.

Tax calendar for the 2026 bill
DateWhat happens
February 28, 2027City payment due, same-day postmark accepted
March 1, 2027City penalty and county 1.5% monthly interest begin
April 5, 2027Deadline to apply for state tax relief or the senior freeze

A house is assessed at 25% of its appraised value, and the rate applies per $100 of that assessed figure. Since tax year 2020 the final bill has been rounded to whole dollars. The Trustee's rate table shows $2.15 per $100 under a 2023 heading, an old figure, so rely on the rate printed on your 2026 notice.

Houses inside city limits also pay a city rate, added to the county one; City Finance can give today's figure. Washington County values rose in 2024, so plenty of owners saw a new appraisal that year. Before listing, pull your latest notice and compare the assessed value with what comparable houses are selling for. If the number looks off, the appeal steps below explain where to go, and the county board of equalization meets in June, so plan around that month.

sections.h2: If you think the assessment is wrong
sections.html:
Call the Washington County Assessor of Property at 423-753-1671 first. An informal review, if offered, is just a conversation and is not an appeal. The formal first step is the county board of equalization, which meets in June, and skipping it usually makes a disputed value final.

An owner who loses at the county can take the case to the state board, filing by August 1 or 45 days after the county notice went out, whichever is later. On the state appeal page, the strongest proof for a house is a set of comparable sales with the differences explained. Saying the home is overvalued without numbers rarely works, and a jump after a countywide reappraisal is not itself proof of a mistake.

Meanwhile, pay the undisputed share before it turns delinquent, and clear any back taxes from earlier years.

Gather your evidence before June. Comparable sales with the differences explained carry the most weight, and a plain claim of overvaluation carries little. If the house has damage or deferred repairs, photos and a written estimate show the Assessor something concrete.

sections.h2: Who pays if the house sells this winter?
sections.html:
Whoever owned the house on January 1 is listed on the tax roll, which means a seller can still get the bill after selling in the fall. Closings normally prorate the tax, and the buyer takes it over from there. Payoffs are requested by the closing agent from both the city and the Trustee, then paid from the seller's proceeds.

If a bill is already late, get the payoff from the tax office itself, because online balances can lag payments in transit. An account sent to Chancery Court is paid through the Clerk and Master rather than the city's website.

If you owe a balance, call 423-434-6299 for the city number, ask the Trustee for the county number, deliver both to the title company, and have each payoff itemized on the settlement statement. A cash sale that closes quickly can clear those balances at the table, which helps when an inherited or tenant-occupied house has fallen behind. A cash buyer does not need a lender to approve the property first, so an overdue tax account does not hold up the schedule the way it can with a financed purchase, as long as the payoff is settled at closing.

Documents worth gathering before you list: your most recent city notice, your county notice if one came, the parcel ID, and the name of the escrow servicer if a lender pays your tax. With those, the title company can request both payoffs without delay.

East Tennessee State University, Ballad Health and the medical campus around Johnson City Medical Center anchor the local economy and support steady rental demand. The city counted 74,943 people in July 2025, 5.5% above 2020. Owners live in about 51.3% of homes, so roughly half of households rent, and a seller may well be a landlord with tenants in place. Median owner-occupied value is $268,200, rent is near $1,023 a month, and household income is near $57,254. For a rental, get the city and county balances before you sign an offer.

Older houses here face about 45 inches of rain and roughly 16 inches of snow a year, which is hard on roofs, gutters and crawl spaces, and a buyer's inspection will start there.

faqs.q: When does the 2026 Johnson City tax bill go late?
faqs.a: It goes late after February 28, 2027. A postmark from that day counts as on time, and penalty and interest begin March 1, 2027. The county Trustee takes payments through the end of February as well.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Johnson City property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the balance is current, with a 2.75% processing fee on each transaction. For delinquent accounts or taxes filed in Chancery Court, call 423-434-6299 for the payoff.

faqs.q: What if no county tax notice ever showed up?
faqs.a: Phone the Washington County Trustee at 423-753-1602. The tax remains owed without a notice, so call as soon as you notice it is missing.

faqs.q: Does Johnson City tax apply to houses in Carter or Sullivan County?
faqs.a: The city bills its own tax inside its limits in any county, while the county portion goes to that county's trustee. Find the county on your parcel record and ask that county's assessor and trustee for dates and rates.

faqs.q: Can a Johnson City house with back taxes be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. Overdue city and county balances are paid from the seller's proceeds, with a current payoff from the tax office supplied to the title company.
